record.title: Meta reports survey estimate of AI-assisted holiday shopping in Mexico
record.summary: Meta’s Spanish-language newsroom summary of an Ipsos-commissioned 2025 holiday-shopping survey reports that more than one in four Mexican year-end shoppers used AI to guide purchase decisions. Meta says the online survey included 942 respondents in Mexico and was fielded across 18 markets in November 2025. The full survey and exact question wording were not accessible, so the statistic remains a source-reported result rather than a verified measure of current Mexican consumer behavior.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Meta published a Spanish-language summary on 22 October 2026 of an Ipsos-commissioned online holiday-shopping survey. Meta says the survey covered 14,473 respondents across 18 markets, including 942 in Mexico, and was fielded 5–19 November 2025; its page says samples were representative by age and gender in each market.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Meta’s summary says more than one in four Mexican year-end shoppers used AI to guide purchase decisions. The underlying survey questionnaire and full country results were not accessible in this review.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The survey does not establish current 2026 prevalence, causal effects of AI on purchases or sales, or the separate revenue and efficiency figures cited elsewhere in Meta’s article from Linux Foundation research.

evidence_gaps.description: The full Ipsos study, question wording, response rates and detailed country tables were not accessible from Meta’s page.
The fieldwork occurred in November 2025; this summary does not establish 2026 consumer behavior or causal business outcomes.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported result is valid for its stated 2025 holiday-shopping sample, AI-assisted purchase decisions among Mexican consumers could inform research and business choices about AI-mediated commerce. Its regional and seasonal scope is meaningful but limited.
limitations: The evidence is Meta’s Spanish-language summary of a company-commissioned online survey; the full Ipsos instrument and results were not accessible.
The survey was fielded 5–19 November 2025 and does not establish current 2026 prevalence.
The statement that more than one in four buyers used AI to guide purchase decisions is attributed to Meta’s survey summary; question wording and denominator are not exposed on the page.
Meta’s separate claims about AI-related business revenue and efficiency cite Linux Foundation research, not this Ipsos survey; no causal effect is established.

technical.claimed_result: Meta reports that more than one in four Mexican year-end shoppers used AI to guide purchase decisions in an Ipsos-commissioned survey fielded in November 2025.
technical.demonstrated_result: Meta published the Spanish-language survey summary on 22 October 2026 and states the sample, Mexico subsample and fieldwork dates.
technical.implementation_status: Survey findings published as a company newsroom summary; underlying report was not accessible in this review.
technical.mechanism: Respondent-reported holiday-shopping behavior, as summarized by Meta; no intervention or causal effect was evaluated.
technical.novelty: A Mexico-specific reported estimate of AI use in seasonal shopping from a multi-market 2025 survey.
technical.regime: Mexico subsample n=942 within an online survey of 14,473 shoppers across 18 markets, fielded 5–19 November 2025.
technical.reproducibility: Full survey instrument and results were not accessible; the reported statistic cannot be independently reconstructed from the summary.
technical.strongest_baseline: No comparable earlier or current survey was inspected.

brief.title: Meta reports survey estimate of AI-assisted holiday shopping in Mexico
brief.why_it_matters: A bounded estimate of reported AI-assisted shopping behavior could inform research and business decisions about AI-mediated commerce in Mexico. The result comes from a company-commissioned 2025 survey summary; it is not a measure of current prevalence or evidence that AI increased sales.
